quote: Binaere Formen mit mehreren verschieden transformirten Variabeln. Aufstellung der Bedingung für das Zerfallen [-nach-] {+in+} etwa dem folgenden Ausdruck:
english: Binary forms with several differently transformed variables. Establishing the condition for decomposition into, for instance, the following expression:
topic: A list of research notes: treating certain functions by analogy with Eisenstein's work on the p-function via infinite products, addition theorems for p and σ, turning covariant criteria into invariant ones, decomposition conditions for binary forms in several variables, vanishing of transvectants, Klein's topic of a typical representation of the Kummer surface, and termination of chains of transvection processes.

triage.modern_statement: The note is about multi-binary forms. These are polynomials F(x^(1),…,x^(k)) that are separately homogeneous in several pairs of binary variables, with each pair acted on by its own SL2 (or GL2). Hilbert wants the invariant-theoretic condition (covariants or concomitants that vanish) for such a form to split into a product or expression of a given shape. The shape was meant to be written right after 'etwa dem folgenden Ausdruck', but the transcription does not include it. The most natural reading is splitting into a product of factors, one per variable series. For multilinear forms this is the rank-one (decomposable) tensor case, i.e. the Segre variety. Without the missing expression, the exact target shape cannot be pinned down.
triage.answered_by: No single answer exists, because the target expression is missing. I can only point to answers for the closest special cases. Splitting into rank-one products: the equations of the Segre variety are the 2×2 minors of the flattenings (classical, from Segre; see modern surveys such as Ottaviani's hyperdeterminant notes). The one-variable analogues: Brill and Gordan gave equations for a form to be a product of linear forms (Brill's equations / the Chow variety), and Hilbert's 1886 Math. Ann. paper treated a binary form being a perfect power (Hilbert covariants).

evidence.claim: The equations of the Segre variety (decomposable multilinear forms or tensors) are the 2×2 minors of the flattening or contraction maps. This is the modern answer to 'when does a multilinear form split into a product of linear forms, one in each variable series'.

The Chow variety of polynomials that split into products of linear forms has been studied for more than 100 years. Brill, Gordan and others found set-theoretic equations for it, and modern work (Guan) computes Brill's equations as a GL(V)-module.
Hilbert's short 1886 Math. Ann. paper asked what conditions make a form of degree n=μν a perfect power. Modern work describes Hilbert covariants that vanish exactly on perfect powers.
A 2026 arXiv note discusses Hilbert's 1886 four-page paper on when a form of degree μν is a perfect power.

triage.why: The note breaks off before the expression Hilbert intended ('etwa dem folgenden Ausdruck:'), so the specific splitting problem can't be identified. The general theme is a recognisable 1880s invariant-theory topic: covariant conditions for a form to split into a given shape. I could not find any source tying a published result to this particular multi-binary problem from the diary. For the closest special cases there are classical and modern answers (Segre-variety equations for rank-one multilinear forms, Brill–Gordan equations, Hilbert's own perfect-power covariants), and research on equations for Chow, Segre and secant varieties is still active. Whether Hilbert's intended problem is among these cases, I can't tell from the sources.
